# What only a person does

An agent is refused these whatever its role, with `operation_forbidden`, the sentence below and the place a person does it (`place`, its link `href` from `site_context.urls.places`). Hand the person the link; never do it another way.

| Act | Also refused | Place | Says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mail.update` |  | `settings.email` | An agent cannot set how this site sends email, whatever its role: the setting holds a password and reroutes every message at once. An administrator sets it in Settings › Email; read it with mail.read and test it with mail.test. Hand them its link: urls.places["settings.email"] in site_context. |
| `site.delete` |  | `home` | An agent cannot delete a site, whatever its role: its pages, files and history go for good. An administrator deletes it, typing its name, in the websites list. Hand them its link: urls.places["home"] in site_context. |
| `package.export` | `site.export`, `site.import`, every `package.*` | `home` | An agent cannot export or import a site package, whatever its role: the whole site leaves or arrives as one file. An administrator does it in the websites list; site.duplicate copies a site. Hand them its link: urls.places["home"] in site_context. |
| `team.manage` | every `team.*` | `account.team` | An agent cannot add people, change their roles or manage workspaces, whatever its role: what it grants would outlive its own token. A person does it in Account › People and access. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.team"] in site_context. |
| `user.manage` | every `user.*` | `account.users` | An agent cannot add people, change their roles or manage workspaces, whatever its role: what it grants would outlive its own token. A person does it in Account › Users. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.users"] in site_context. |
| `workspace.manage` | every `workspace.*`, every `program.*` | `account.workspaces` | An agent cannot add people, change their roles or manage workspaces, whatever its role: what it grants would outlive its own token. A person does it in Account › Workspaces. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.workspaces"] in site_context. |
| `accessRequest.manage` | every `accessRequest.*` | `account.access-requests` | An agent cannot add people, change their roles or manage workspaces, whatever its role: what it grants would outlive its own token. A person does it in Account › Access requests. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.access-requests"] in site_context. |
| `agentToken.manage` | every `agentToken.*` | `account.agents` | An agent cannot make, change or revoke agent tokens, whatever its role: a token it made would outlive its own. A person does it in Account › Agents. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.agents"] in site_context. |
| `submission.export` | `submission.csv`, `submission.download` | `forms` | An agent cannot download a form's messages as a file, whatever its role: they are visitors' personal data. A person downloads them in Forms; read them a page at a time with submission.list. Hand them its link: urls.places["forms"] in site_context. |
| `ticket.triage` | `ticket.update`, `ticket.close` | `account.reports` | An agent cannot triage or close reports, whatever its role: the people who run Libretto answer them. They do it in Account › Reports; read your own with the reports resource. Hand them its link: urls.places["account.reports"] in site_context. |
